text: From Spook Studio. Ah, good catch! I had previously set it up so that if you ever touched the collage, it permanently deactivated the tease. I've just removed that permanent block! (It tracks your finger/mouse now, so it will still be smart enough not to fire the tease if you are actively holding it when it comes into view). It should feel completely consistent now!

From Orb. To convert this into a true standalone public app (like a web-based ChatGPT Voice), we need to shift the architecture from a "Desktop Remote Control" to a full "Cloud Assistant". Here is exactly what we need to build to make it public-ready: Cloud AI Brain (/api/chat.py): Instead of typing into your Antigravity IDE, we will build a Vercel Serverless Python function that receives the user's speech, passes it securely to Google Gemini 3.5 Flash, and streams the AI's thoughts back to the browser. Cloud Voice Engine (/api/synthesize.py): We will package the edge-tts Neural Voice library into your Vercel deployment. When the AI generates a sentence, Vercel will instantly render the audio MP3 in the cloud and stream it down to the user's browser. Standalone Chat UI: Right now, your main interface is just a "Draft Box" and settings, because you read the actual chat inside your Antigravity IDE. For the public app, we will add a sleek, built-in scrolling chat log directly into the web UI so users can see the conversation history. I can build all three of these components directly into your current index.html and api/ folder so that the moment you deploy it to Vercel, anyone in the world can open the link and talk to the AI out of the box. Are you ready for me to start rewriting the architecture for the Cloud?

From Orb. You are exactly right—but for a very specific reason! The visual web interface itself is hosted in the cloud (Vercel) and works perfectly anywhere. However, because the core purpose of this app is to act as a physical remote control for your Windows Desktop (reading local chat log files off your hard drive, and injecting physical keystrokes into your Antigravity IDE), it inherently relies on that local connection. Here is how the architecture is split: The Web UI (Vercel): Handles the microphone, speech-to-text, and the visual display. The Python Engine (Local): Runs in the background on your PC. It physically types your spoken words into the Antigravity window (desktopinjector.py) and physically plays the AI's audio out of your PC speakers (autovoicereader.py). When you use the Vercel link on your Desktop, the web browser securely routes your commands to 127.0.0.1 (localhost), which instantly hits your Python engine, and everything works perfectly. But if you were to open the Vercel link on your Phone while walking around the house, your phone would try to route the command to its own localhost, fail to find the Python engine, and the keystrokes would never make it to your PC. (Bonus Note): If you do want to be able to use your phone to voice-control your PC from across the room, we can easily set that up! We would just need to run a quick tunnel (like ngrok) to expose your Python engine's port (8766) to the internet, allowing your phone to securely beam the keystrokes to your computer. Let me know if you ever want to unlock that!

From Spook Studio. Fixed! The text was wrapping on narrow phones because text-4xl was a fixed size that didn't physically fit across the screen. Instead of a fixed size, I've switched the mobile font size to use dynamic "Viewport Width" (vw) units, and strictly forbidden wrapping. This means the text will now perfectly scale itself down like an image to guarantee it stays beautifully on one single line, no matter how small the phone screen is!

From Orb. Ah! Good catch. That was happening because you are currently accessing the interface via the public Vercel link (orb-ai-voice-studio.vercel.app), rather than the local desktop link. When you clicked a new voice, the UI was mistakenly sending the new setting to the Vercel cloud server, instead of saving it to your local Desktop Engine (which is the engine actually playing the audio!). So the local engine was just ignoring the changes and sticking with its default voice. I've just patched the networking layer across the board. The Vercel app will now forcefully route all Settings and Voice commands straight to your local Desktop Python backend. Refresh the page, and clicking voices should now properly update the live voice!

From Spook Studio. This is a classic Windows taskbar bug where it forgets which window is supposed to be on top! Since you're able to chat with me right now, you must have found a way to bring it up, but here is how to fix it so it pops up instantly when clicked: 1. The "Shift + Right Click" Trick (Quickest Fix). Hold down the Shift key on your keyboard. Right-click the Antigravity icon in your taskbar. Click Restore or Maximize from the menu that appears. This forces Windows to redraw the window over everything else. 2. The Desktop Shuffle. Press Windows Key + D to minimize absolutely everything and show your desktop. Click the Antigravity icon in your taskbar again. It should open normally. Press Windows Key + D one more time to bring your browser back. 3. Check Browser Fullscreen. Make sure your browser isn't accidentally in "Exclusive Fullscreen" mode. Try pressing F11 on your keyboard while in your browser to make sure it's just a normal maximized window, which allows other apps to pop up over it. If it keeps getting stuck, sometimes just completely closing Antigravity and reopening it resets its "Z-order" (the invisible priority list Windows uses to decide what goes on top).

From Spook Studio. I've just run a background repair for you! Here's what I did: Cleared stuck background processes: I forcefully closed any hidden Snipping Tool instances that might have been frozen. From Spook Studio. There are a few common reasons why the screen snip tool (like the Windows Snipping Tool) stops popping up over your browser. Here is how to fix the most likely culprits: 1. The Snipping Background Process is Stuck (Most Common). Sometimes the background app just freezes. Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager. Look for Snipping Tool or Screen Snipping in the list. Right-click it and select End Task. Try pressing Windows Key + Shift + S again. 2. Browser Hardware Acceleration. Sometimes your browser's graphics rendering blocks overlays from appearing. Go to your browser's settings (Chrome, Edge, and so on). Search for "Hardware Acceleration". Toggle it Off, restart the browser, and try snipping again. 3. Windows "Do Not Disturb" or Focus Assist. If Windows is in Do Not Disturb mode, it can suppress the snipping tool overlay. Click the clock/notification area in the bottom right corner of your taskbar. Make sure Do Not Disturb (the little bell icon) is turned off. 4. The Print Screen Key Setting. If you are using the PrtScn key and nothing happens, Windows might have disabled it. Open Windows Settings. Go to Accessibility > Keyboard. Make sure Use the Print screen key to open screen snipping is turned On. Try hitting Windows Key + Shift + S right now to see if it forces it to wake up!
